rv.q: Phelim McDermott's production is full of invention, with neat puppetry and plenty of cheeky, lo-fi vibrancy.

The danger is that amidst all this bonhomie, and with Broadbent’s Scrooge so essentially loveable and baby-faced even when supposedly at his most curmudgeonly, the story’s backbone – its redemptive arc – is lost.
The perfect, West End, family treat.
This beautifully conceived tale of redemption and goodwill retains all its ghostly power to thrill, and with Broadbent at the helm, it’s glorious family entertainment for Christmas.
Pye's costumes are an eyeful and the whole thing's as luscious as it is ludicrous.

cn.t: Broadbent's detailed performance anchors this playful, toy-theatre adaptation that sends up Victorian stagecraft while preserving the story's heart, though some find Scrooge too genial for a proper miser.
